summary: Request timeouts on long-context prompts with large max_tokens (streaming disconnects / 504)
description:
Issue summary: BrightChat reports repeated request timeouts (client sees 504 / streaming disconnects) when sending long-context prompts with large max_tokens. Impact: their chat product is experiencing message send failures for long multi-turn conversations; customer is on enterprise plan and has a production SLA. Environment: prod-us-east, requests go through hosted API, model pinned to gpt-large-v2. Observed since 2026-03-01 after increased usage of >32k token contexts and max_tokens=12000.

High-level hypothesis: timeouts are correlated with long decode times (large max_tokens) and sustained KV cache/allocator pressure causing serving runtime stalls and upstream gateway connection timeouts. Also investigating batching interactions and streaming backlog leading to request lifecycle exceeding gateway/h2 timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: Obtain BrightChat API key (customer-provided) and send a text generation request to /v1/generate with model=gpt-large-v2
Construct a prompt combining ~30k tokens of conversation history (they provided an anonymized example) and set max_tokens=12000, streaming=true
Observe: initial tokens stream for ~15-20s then streaming connection drops with HTTP 504 from our API gateway; repeated attempts show similar behavior. Lowering max_tokens to 2048 removes the issue.
Run same request on dedicated capacity (if available) — BrightChat cannot easily test; asked to confirm.

investigation_notes: 03/02 Priya: Reproduced locally with synthetic 28k-token prompt; observed streaming disconnect after ~20s when simulated max_tokens=12000. Lowering max_tokens reduces decoding time and no disconnects seen.

03/02 Evan (SRE): Heap/allocator logs show repeated large contiguous allocations during decode with our quantized kernels; concurrent requests with batching increase memory churn. Potential interaction between large KV cache growth and GC in the runtime.

03/03 Priya: Noted api-gateway default upstream idle timeout is 30s for h2; some customers with long decodes hit that. We have fallback logic but streaming session lifecycles may not refresh the idle timer correctly for active token streaming when buffer backpressure is present.

03/03 Support: Customer confirmed they started using much larger conversation histories and an experimental summary-preserve strategy; spike in average max_tokens across their calls from 1.5k to ~10k.

03/04 Engineering: Added instrumentation to track per-request decode time, bytes-in-flight, and batch sizes. Early data shows long requests are often batched with unrelated short requests, increasing end-to-end latency for the long request due to scheduler coalescing.
comments: 2026-03-02 Diego Ramirez (Support): Opened ticket on behalf of BrightChat after they reported 504s for long conversations. Customer impact: production chat outages for certain users. Asked for request_id and example payload — provided.
2026-03-02 Priya Nair (Support Eng): Acknowledged ticket, asked for full anonymized prompt and whether they can test with streaming=false. Assigned to SRE for deeper runtime tracing.

2026-03-03 Evan Brooks (SRE): Collected runtime traces; observed allocator stalls and batching coalescing issues. Proposed immediate mitigation: lower api-gateway upstream idle timeout? (No) — better to adjust scheduler to avoid coalescing long decodes with short requests and ensure streaming heartbeats update upstream timers.

2026-03-03 BrightChat (Customer): Provided anonymized conversation history and confirmed they can temporarily reduce max_tokens to 2048 as a stopgap but need a long-term fix since they rely on long context for session recall.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair: Scoped short-term workarounds for customer: (1) recommend client-side increase of HTTP client timeout to 120s and enable reconnect/resume logic, (2) set max_tokens <= 4096 for calls routed through hosted API, or request Dedicated capacity where runtime knob tuning is available. Added internal follow-ups for engineering.
2026-03-04 Evan Brooks: Created INT-904 to track scheduler fix; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1284 for batching heuristic change and streaming keepalive fixes.
resolution: Workarounds provided to customer: (1) temporarily reduce max_tokens to <=4096 or use summarization to shrink prompt, (2) increase client-side HTTP timeout and implement streaming reconnect/append logic. Engineering follow-ups: change scheduler batching heuristics to avoid coalescing long decodes with short requests (PR linked), ensure streaming heartbeats update api-gateway timers, and investigate allocator/GC behavior under large KV cache growth. Target patch scheduled for 2026-03-10 on canary with metrics monitored.
